Bulletin 489 Termination of Agency Relationships and Maine’s Cancellation Control Acts It has come to the Bureau’s attention that some Maine consumers have recently had their homeowners, renters, or personal auto policies nonrenewed solely because the insurer’s agency relationship with a producer has terminated. This is not a lawful basis for nonrenewal.
Insurers are reminded that in Maine, these lines of business are subject to Cancellation Control Acts that grant policyholders the right to renew their policies unless the insurer can demonstrate a valid reason for nonrenewal. The only permissible reasons for nonrenewal are those specified in the Maine Automobile Insurance Cancellation Control Act1 or the Maine Property Cancellation Control Act,2 as applicable. For all policies that are subject to either Control Act, the reason or reasons for nonrenewal action must be explicitly stated in the notice of nonrenewal. Vague explanations such as “underwriting reasons” are insufficient.3
Producers who no longer represent a particular insurer are free to offer policyholders alternative coverage with a different insurer, but that does not extinguish the policyholders’ right to renew the coverage they have. entry.title: Attention Trading Partners: Take Action Now Before MaineCare’s New Online Portal Goes Live
entry.content:

  • Help |

DHHS → Office of MaineCare Services (OMS) → Provider Resources → Attention Trading Partners: Take Action Now Before MaineCare’s New Online Portal Goes Live

Attention Trading Partners: Take Action Now Before MaineCare’s New Online Portal Goes Live

Aug 03, 2026

A refreshed and upgraded MIHMS is coming in mid October 2026. The Office of MaineCare Services (OMS), in partnership with Gainwell Technologies, is launching an upgraded MIHMS, to bring enhanced security, improved usability, and a more modern experience to better support your day-to-day work.

The upgrade will include a new “MaineCare Partner Portal” that will replace what is known today as the “Health PAS Online Portal.” Please note that, until the October go-live, we will continue using the name “Health PAS Online Portal” in communications related to current functionality.

You can read more about the benefits to providers and members on the Health PAS Online Portal.

Trading Partners Preparation

This message is part of a series about changes to how trading partners will access the new portal and what you must do now to prepare for these changes.

Trading partners include providers, billing agents, health plans, clearinghouses, and business associates. Trading partners have an important role to play in supporting a smooth transition and uninterrupted access to the portal after go-live.

Portal Access Impacts and Required Actions Before Go‑Live

The preparation activities and changes below will improve system security by ensuring the right people have the right access, at go-live and ongoing. Most actions are only for Admin (R7) users.

Most important: Providers with duplicate emails need to make changes to their portal user accounts now to assist with account migration to the upgraded portal. On September 1, we will terminate current Admin (R7) user accounts that share an email address with another user account. We will not terminate Admin (R7) user accounts if they are the only Admin (R7) on the Trading Partner account.

If a user account is terminated and they still need portal access, another user with Admin Rights (R7) can invite the terminated user using a unique email address, not the one previously used.

Activity/Change

Your Action

Why it Matters

What’s Next?

At go-live, MaineCare will only migrate Admin (R7) accounts to the new portal.

 

MaineCare will not migrate inactive accounts.

Designate at least one active Admin (R7) per organization, and two for backup coverage.

 

Trading Partners with large user populations should plan for sufficient Admin (R7) coverage to avoid access delays after go-live; we recommend one Admin (R7) per 25 users.

 

Remove inactive Admin (R7) accounts.

After go-live, Admin (R7) users will need to re-invite all other active users. More Admin (R7) users mean less re-invitation work for each user.

 

Trading Partners have an existing and ongoing responsibility to remove inactive users to help keep our systems and data secure.

 

We will monitor the number and activity of Admin (R7) users per Trading Partner and will reach out to individual Trading Partners if needed.

In the new portal, your username will be your email address.

MaineCare will not migrate accounts that share an email address.

Confirm that each active Admin (R7) user account has its own unique email address.

OMS will deactivate accounts that continue to share email addresses as we approach go-live.

After go-live, Admin (R7) users will need immediate access to the portal to invite other users and avoid disruption in Trading Partner work.

We will monitor accounts that share email addresses and will reach out to individual Trading Partners if needed.

Admin (R7) users will invite other users to the portal and designate your roles after go-live.

 

Admin (R7) will be able to choose from ~40 permissions, compared to 9 today.

Prepare to invite users after go-live:

  • Know who needs a user account in the new portal
  • Know the permission level each user will need to have

 

Admin (R7) users will need to invite other users shortly after go-live to avoid a disruption in Trading Partner work.

 

We will share more information during trainings including role definitions, templates, and other guidance.

 

For questions, please email Provider Services or call 1-866-690-5585.

entry.content:

DHHS → Office of MaineCare Services (OMS) → Provider Resources → Provider Responsibility Regarding Third Party Liability and Secondary Billing

Provider Responsibility Regarding Third Party Liability and Secondary Billing

Aug 03, 2026

In a previous notice, the Office of MaineCare Services (OMS) reminded providers of your responsibilities regarding third -party liability and secondary billing. Pursuant to MaineCare Benefits Manual (MBM) Ch. I Section 1.07-3(B), MaineCare is the payor of last resort. OMS announced that we will update the billing and claims system requirements to accurately reflect the provider’s obligation to bill primary insurance when other coverage is available.

Effective August 10, 2026, our claims system will no longer treat most Current Procedural Terminology (CPT) and Healthcare Common Procedure Coding System (HCPCS) codes as exempt from billing the primary commercial carrier. In accordance with MBM Ch. I Section 1.07: Third Party Liability, providers must seek payment from the primary carrier before billing MaineCare for all claims for these services for members with primary coverage, even when:

  • the billing codes for same services vary between payors; and
  • the primary payor’s service coverage applies only to a portion of the MaineCare defined service. For example, this applies when the MaineCare service is more comprehensive than the primary payor’s coverage.

MaineCare also recognizes that many provider types that were previously unable to enroll in Medicare can now enroll and bill Medicare as the primary payor for services delivered to members dually eligible for Medicare and Medicaid. Providers eligible to enroll with Medicare to deliver Medicare reimbursable services must do so to receive MaineCare reimbursement as a secondary payor.

MaineCare’s claims system will accept an Explanation of Benefits (EOB) with primary dollars attached even if the billing codes differ. The system will process secondary claims as long as the provider, member, dates of service, and billed charges match. Providers must use the most specific code possible to maintain billing integrity and to comply with correct claim submission procedures.

Please monitor MaineCare e-messages for future communications on this topic as continued reviews and necessary system changes occur. We appreciate your efforts to preserve MaineCare funding and ensure compliance with these requirements.

For questions, please contact your Provider Relations Specialist.

entry.content:

DHHS → Office of MaineCare Services (OMS) → Provider Resources → New MaineCare Partner Portal Training for Trading Partners

New MaineCare Partner Portal Training for Trading Partners

Aug 04, 2026

We previously shared that a refreshed and upgraded MIHMS, with a new “MaineCare Partner Portal,” is coming in October 2026. This will replace the current HealthPAS Online Portal. We are now inviting trading partners to register for training starting September 8, 2026, to help you prepare for the transition to the new portal. 

Gainwell Technologies will be leading live virtual instructor-led training sessions. These courses will provide the knowledge and skills needed to navigate the new portal, complete daily business functions, and use new portal features. Training demonstrations, materials, and supporting resources will help participants prepare for a successful transition. 

Steps You Need to Take to Attend Training

  • Review the available training topics listed below and identify the sessions that align with your role and responsibilities. 

  • Use the Learning Management System (LMS) registration to create an account, access the training catalog, and enroll in applicable sessions. See the instructions below for guidance in registering. 

  • Contact Gainwell (instructions below) if you need assistance. 

  • Recorded sessions and other training materials will be available in the LMS after training sessions for ongoing reference. 

MaineCare Partner Portal Training Sessions 

Course Name 

Description 

ME - TPT - Migrated Trading Partner Log In and Account Maintenance Training (ILC) 

Learn how to complete first-time login activities, configure multi-factor authentication (MFA), manage user accounts and permissions, perform account maintenance activities, and understand electronic data interchange (EDI) certification requirements and status monitoring. This course is only for Admin (R7) users. 

ME - TPT - Trading Partner Registration and Account Maintenance Training (ILC) 

Learn how to register a new Trading Partner account, complete account activation, manage users and permissions, associate providers and billing agents, navigate the portal, and maintain account information.  

ME - TPT - Authorization, Referrals and Certifications Training (ILC) 

Learn how to submit and manage authorizations, process referrals, monitor certification requests and statuses, and access related portal functionality.dr 

ME - TPT - Dental Claim Entry & Claim Management Training (ILC) 

Learn how to submit dental claims, monitor claim processing and status, and navigate claim-related portal functions. 

ME - TPT - Institutional Claim Entry & Claim Management Training (ILC) 

Learn how to submit institutional claims, monitor claim processing and status, and navigate claim-related portal functions. 

ME - TPT - Professional Claim Entry & Claim Management Training (ILC) 

Learn how to submit professional claims, monitor claim status, review payment information, access remittance advice, and complete related claim activities. 

ME - TPT - MaineCare Partner Public Portal Training (ILC) 

Learn about publicly available portal functionality, portal resources and reference materials, secure messaging, Trading Partner tools, and available resources. 

LMS Access and Course Registration Instructions 

Use the following steps to register for MaineCare Partner Portal training. Multiple sessions are available for each course to allow for scheduling flexibility. 

  1. Go to the LMS registration site: https://mmislearningcenter.myabsorb.com/#/login. 

  1. Sign in using your existing account or click Sign Up on the right side of the window to create a new account. 

  1. If you need a new account, enter the enrollment key: De8pO9CBYXYB-aOCY8qp on the Sign Up window. 

  1. Complete the required registration information to create your account. You can enter your workplace address. 

  1. The Learner Dashboard appears. From this window, you can access previous trainings, search for and enroll in the appropriate training sessions, and review your transcript. 

  1. To locate the appropriate courses, search using “TPT” or the course name from the table above in the search bar at the top of the window or by opening the Course Catalog tile. 

  1. Click Choose Session for each course you need to complete, then enroll in the session that best fits your schedule.  

  1. You will receive an email confirmation regarding the success of your enrollment. Additionally, you will receive a Microsoft Teams calendar event for each session.  

  1. On the day of the training, access the training via one of the following methods: 

  • Access the Teams Meeting hyperlink from the course confirmation email. 

  • Click the Microsoft Teams meeting hyperlink within the Outlook/Teams calendar event. 

  • Access My Courses in the LMS and click the appropriate Microsoft Teams meeting hyperlink.

entry.title: US Department of Labor finds child labor and wage violations at 3 San Antonio bakery and café locations
entry.content: SAN ANTONIO – The U.S. Department of Labor has recovered thousands in back wages and assessed penalties after a federal investigation revealed child labor, minimum wage, and overtime violations by the operators of three La Panaderia Bakery & Café locations in San Antonio.The department’s Wage and Hour Division investigated the pay practices of Tequila Almond Croissant LLC, Pan Dulce LLC, and SA Bakery Co. LLC. All three do business as La Panaderia Bakery & Café in San Antonio with locations at 301 E. Houston Street; 17030 Fiesta Texas Drive; and 8305 Broadway.Division investigators found the employers violated child labor provisions of the Fair Labor Standards Act. Specifically, they employed a 13-year-old minor who was under the legal age for employment and permitted a 15-year-old minor to work overnight, which is prohibited for 14- and 15-year-olds. The division assessed a $25,706 civil money penalty for the child labor violations.The division’s investigation also revealed minimum wage violations due to the employers’ failure to pay one worker for two overnight shifts at the La Cantera café location on Fiesta Texas Drive. The employers also failed to combine hours for employees who worked at multiple café locations and paid the employees straight-time rates instead of the required time-and-one-half overtime rates. Employers and workers can contact the division with questions and requests for compliance assistance at its toll-free helpline, 866-4US-WAGE (487-9243). Employers are also encouraged to use the agency’s industry-specific compliance assistance toolkits to learn about their responsibilities under the laws enforced by the division. The agency’s PAID program offers employers an opportunity to self-report and resolve potential minimum wage and overtime violations under the FLSA, as well as certain potential violations under the Family and Medical Leave Act.Download the agency’s free timesheet app for iOS and Android devices to track hours and pay.

entry.title: US Department of Labor finds urgent care employer failed to pay over $113K in owed wages to workers for required orientation, meetings, training
entry.content: ATLANTA – The U.S. Department of Labor has recovered $113,199 in back wages after an investigation found a Richmond Hill urgent care facility failed to pay its workers for hours worked and retaliated against a worker for questioning its pay practices.An investigation by the department’s Wage and Hour Division found that Premier Health Consultants LLC – operating as St. Joseph Candler Urgent Care – violated the Fair Labor Standards Act by paying straight time instead of time and one-half in overtime for all hours worked over 40 when employees were required to attend mandatory orientation, meetings, and training. The employer also required certain employees to work off the clock, resulting in unpaid overtime, and suspended a worker who questioned pay practices, all violations of the FLSA.Workers and employers can call the Wage and Hour Division with questions and requests for compliance assistance at its toll-free helpline, 866-4US-WAGE (487-9243). Employers are encouraged to use the agency’s industry-specific compliance assistance toolkits to learn about their responsibilities under the laws enforced by the division. The agency’s PAID program offers employers an opportunity to self-report and resolve potential minimum wage and overtime violations under the FLSA, as well as certain potential violations under the Family and Medical Leave Act. Learn more about the Wage and Hour Division, including a search tool that workers can use if they think they may be owed back wages collected by the division. Download the agency’s free timesheet app for iOS and Android devices to track hours and pay.

Attention Trading Partners: Training for New MaineCare Partner Portal

Aug 12, 2026

We have previously shared that a refreshed and upgraded MIHMS, with a new “MaineCare Partner Portal,” is coming in October 2026. This will replace the current HealthPAS Online Portal. We are now inviting trading partners to register for training starting September 8, 2026 to help you prepare for the transition to the new portal.

Gainwell Technologies will be leading live virtual instructor-led training sessions. These courses will provide the knowledge and skills needed to navigate the new portal, complete daily business functions, and use new portal features. Training demonstrations, materials, and supporting resources will help participants prepare for a successful transition.

Steps you need to take to attend training

  • Review the available training topics listed below and identify the sessions that align with your role and responsibilities.
  • Use the LMS registration (instructions below) to create an account, access the training catalog, and enroll in applicable sessions.
  • Contact Gainwell (instructions below) if you need assistance.
  • Recorded sessions and other training materials will be available in the LMS after training sessions for ongoing reference.

MaineCare Partner Portal Training Sessions

Course Name

Description

ME - TPT - Migrated Trading Partner Log In and Account Maintenance Training (ILC)

Learn how to complete first-time login activities, configure multi-factor authentication (MFA), manage user accounts and permissions, perform account maintenance activities, and understand electronic data interchange (EDI) certification requirements and status monitoring. This course is only for Admin (R7) users.

ME - TPT - Trading Partner Registration and Account Maintenance Training (ILC)

Learn how to register a new Trading Partner account, complete account activation, manage users and permissions, associate providers and billing agents, navigate the portal, and maintain account information.

ME - TPT - Authorization, Referrals and Certifications Training (ILC)

Learn how to submit and manage authorizations, process referrals, monitor certification requests and statuses, and access related portal functionality.

ME - TPT - Dental Claim Entry & Claim Management Training (ILC)

Learn how to submit dental claims, monitor claim processing and status, and navigate claim-related portal functions.

ME - TPT - Institutional Claim Entry & Claim Management Training (ILC)

Learn how to submit institutional claims, monitor claim processing and status, and navigate claim-related portal functions.

ME - TPT - Professional Claim Entry & Claim Management Training (ILC)

Learn how to submit professional claims, monitor claim status, review payment information, access remittance advice, and complete related claim activities.

ME - TPT - MaineCare Partner Public Portal Training (ILC)

Learn about publicly available portal functionality, portal resources and reference materials, secure messaging, Trading Partner tools, and available resources.

 

LMS Access and Course Registration Instructions

Use the following steps to register for MaineCare Partner Portal training. Multiple sessions are available for each course to allow for scheduling flexibility.

  1. Go to the LMS registration site: https://mmislearningcenter.myabsorb.com/#/login.
  2. Sign in using your existing account or click Sign Up on the right side of the window to create a new account.
  3. If you need a new account, enter the enrollment key: De8pO9CBYXYB-aOCY8qp on the Sign Up window.
  4. Complete the required registration information to create your account. Note: You can enter your workplace address.
  5. The Learner Dashboard appears. From this window, you can access previous trainings, search for and enroll in the appropriate training sessions, and review your transcript.
  6. To locate the appropriate courses, search using “TPT” or the course name from the table above in the search bar at the top of the window or by opening the Course Catalog tile.
  7. Click Choose Session for each course you need to complete, then enroll in the session that best fits your schedule.
  8. You will receive an email confirmation regarding the success of your enrollment. Additionally, you will receive a Microsoft Teams calendar event for each session.
  9. On the day of the training, access the training via one of the following methods:
    • Access the Teams Meeting hyperlink from the course confirmation email.
    • Click the Microsoft Teams meeting hyperlink within the Outlook/Teams calendar event.
    • Access My Courses in the LMS and click the appropriate Microsoft Teams meeting hyperlink.

Do not forward meeting invitations to other attendees. Each participant must register through the LMS to receive course access, training credit, and post-training evaluation access.

Support Sessions

We are offering optional virtual support sessions during the week of August 17, 2026 to help with LMS access and training registration and to ask questions about upcoming training topics. This helps prevent troubleshooting access issues during the live training. Please contact Jennifer Fehn at Jennifer.Fehn@gainwelltechnologies.com or Haritha Chintada at

Beem fell from her mule and was injured. Beem brought a negligence action against Temple in the Superior Court, and Temple moved for summary judgment, asserting immunity from liability under 7 M.R.S. § 4103-A (2026) and contending that Beem failed to make a prima facie case of negligence. Natural Resources Disaster Relief Assistance Program (NRDRAP) applications Open today, Friday, August 14

August 14, 2026

The Maine Department of Agriculture, Conservation and Forestry (DACF) is opening applications for the Natural Resources Disaster Relief Assistance Program (NRDRAP) today, Friday, August 14, 2026.

Maine farmers, forestry businesses, aquaculture producers, and other eligible producers who experienced weather-related losses in 2023 or 2024 may qualify for financial assistance.

Eligible losses may include crop loss, aquaculture loss, standing timber loss, harvested timber loss, on-farm and forestry infrastructure loss, and bare-ground practices necessary to mitigate land loss.

Application period: August 14, 2026, through November 6, 2026.

Applications will be accepted through the online portal. Paper applications are available upon request.

Producers can prepare now. Applicants are encouraged to begin gathering documentation, including:

  • Ownership or lease documentation
  • Parcel ID information
  • FSA Farm Number, if applicable
  • Tax or business identification information
  • Photos or records documenting damage

Other records related to weather-related losses in 2023 and/or 2024 DACF will provide technical assistance throughout the application period. Virtual office hours will be held every Friday from 11:00 a.m. to 1:00 p.m. beginning August 14.

For updates, eligibility information, and application details, visit maine.gov/dacf/nrdrap, email NRDRA.DACF@maine.gov, or call (207) 530-3144.
